chase_cards.name: No.2 Trainer
chase_cards.why: This is a chase because second place is not a lesser generic trophy; it is its own coordinate in the 2002 circuit. The card names a runner-up, a region, a gendered variant, and a place in a tournament structure that was widening to include Masters.

key_artists.name: Ken Sugimori
key_artists.why: Collector references pin Ken Sugimori to this Battle Road Spring 2002 No.2 Trainer row, while Bulbapedia's Sugimori page supplies the broader art lineage. The authority is useful, but it stays below primary-source strength until a stronger row-level source is attached.

claims.text: The local catalog models Battle Road Spring 2002 regional second place prize as one unnumbered promotional source row containing No.2 Trainer at source index 248.
Bulbapedia says the 2002 No.2 Trainer Battle Road Spring print was awarded to runners-up of each regional Battle Road Spring 2002 tournament, held between March and April 2002.
Bulbapedia says the Battle Road 2002 series was the first to introduce the Master age division for players 18 and over, in addition to Junior and Senior divisions.
Bulbapedia says the 2002 No.2 Trainer versions were the last to include the winner's name and regional conference on the card itself and the last to feature male and female variants.
Bulbapedia gives the Battle Road Spring 2002 No.2 Trainer text as recognizing and praising the second place winner of the Pokémon Card Game Official Tournament 'Battle Road Spring 2002'.
Bulbapedia says the Battle Road Spring 2002 tournaments did not feature a Best in Japan final; top ranking players instead earned byes in Battle Road Summer 2002.
PokeBoon's exact Battle Road Spring 2002 No.2 Trainer page lists Ken Sugimori as illustrator; this is useful collector-reference support, not primary-source print authority.

Pokumon's Battle Road 2002 research reconstructs Spring 2002 No.2 Trainer distribution as 2 girls and 25 boys from Trainers Magazine winner data; this is a collector estimate, not an official copy count.

Bulbapedia's Ken Sugimori page says there are many Pokémon TCG cards illustrated by Sugimori, though most include reused artwork from games, and indexes his broad official artwork role in the franchise.

As judged collector texture, this No.2 Trainer matters because it makes runner-up status legible instead of generic: second place, regional Battle Road Spring 2002, personalized name/conference, gender variant, and the small-N trophy ecology around it.

Agents should preserve No.2 rank, Battle Road Spring 2002 regional runner-up route, source index 248, e-Card Era layout, winner name and regional conference fields, male/female variant boundary, Spring-vs-Summer distinction, and non-equivalence with No.1/No.3 Trainer or other No.2 Trainer eras before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Battle Road Spring 2002 No.2 Trainer: the runner-up still has an address
narrative.why_it_matters: No.2 Trainer is the card that keeps the trophy ladder honest. It refuses the lazy idea that only first place matters. This row is a runner-up object from a specific regional Battle Road Spring 2002 machine, still personalized by name and conference, still split by variant, and still scarce enough that collector research talks in tiny counts. The card's power is not just rank. It is placement made physical.

narrative.human_title: No.2 Trainer, Spring 2002: the runner-up card with a name
narrative.why_it_matters: The No.2 Trainer is easy to flatten if you only chase rank. But second place is a real position in the tournament memory. This card says someone made the final table of a regional Battle Road Spring event, carried a name and conference into the cardboard, and stood inside a tiny variant population that collectors are still reconstructing. The why is not simply scarcity. It is recognition made specific.
